issues.issue: The requirement that any modification or consent be in a writing executed by both parties sits uneasily with Paragraph 3(a), which allows Transactions to be agreed orally, and with Paragraph 13, which allows notices and requests to be made orally.
"[N]o material adverse change in Seller's financial condition" is a deemed representation with no threshold or measure of materiality.

The recognition is qualified by "except insofar as the type of Securities ... or the term ... would render such definition inapplicable", a self-cancelling proviso whose operation is left to be worked out case by case.

This section declares Annexes III-VII and Schedules III.A and VII.A to "form a part of this Agreement and ... be applicable", yet Schedule III.A is a blank "[Insert provisions applicable to relevant country]" template and Schedule VII.A lists no Funds or Custodians, so annexes that presuppose completed schedules are switched on with nothing in them.

This clause says Annex I governs over any inconsistency with "the Agreement", but Annex VI §1 and the conflict sentence in Annex VII each provide that those Annexes prevail over "any other term of the Agreement"; the priority rules are circular.

This section abolishes the Paragraph 5(ii) election that Paragraph 5 of the Agreement expressly confers on Buyer, and Annex VI §9 in turn disapplies Paragraph 5 altogether to Buy/Sell Back Transactions.

"[S]ubstantially the same Securities" is the operative test for permitted substitution and is nowhere defined, and the notice deadline refers to "such business day" with no antecedent day identified. Both leave the mechanics of a substitution notice open to opposing readings.

The subparagraph is triggered where "Seller exercises its right to substitute or terminate under subparagraph (c)", but (c) gives Seller no termination right — it says only that Buyer "shall offer Seller the right to terminate"; the cross-reference does not match the clause it invokes.

The definition is stated to apply "[f]or purposes of the Agreement" but every limb is conditioned on an International Transaction, so "business day" — used throughout Paragraphs 4 and 11 — is left undefined for ordinary domestic Transactions.
Paragraphs 4(c) and 11(iv) of the Agreement impose deadlines by reference to "business day" although this Annex III definition, the only one in the instrument, covers only International Transactions.
"LIBOR plus a spread, as may be specified" leaves the spread open, so if none is specified in a Confirmation the substituted Prime Rate has no determinable value.

The proviso limits the term "Tax" "for purposes of Paragraphs 5 and 6" without saying whether those are Paragraphs 5 and 6 of the Agreement (Income Payments and Security Interest) or of Annex III (Taxes and Tax Event). The cross-reference is genuinely two-way.
"[A]ny circumstance known or reasonably known to it" is an unusual and imprecise formulation of the knowledge standard triggering the notice duty.
The trigger is that the Change of Tax Law will, "in the notifying party's reasonable opinion, have a material adverse effect", combining a subjective opinion with an undefined materiality threshold.

The bar on "any sum constituting consequential loss or damage" uses a term of notoriously contested meaning, and it is not reconciled with the indemnity for "reasonable legal and other professional expenses" in the same sentence.

Paragraph 10(ii) of the Agreement has each party represent that it will act as principal unless agency is agreed in writing in advance, whereas this Annex is declared applicable by Annex I §1 to "all transactions" in which a party acts as agent.
